questions.questionText: hour Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.

The schedule shows the total utility derived by a consumer of a good X at different levels of consumption. quantity of X consumed 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 total utility (units) 30 50 65 75 80 83 84 The consumer obtains two units of utility from the last $ she spends on each good that she purchases. What is the maximum number of units of X that she will consume if the price of X is $5?
In the diagram a consumer’s budget line shifts from GH to JK. J G good Y O K H good X Which statement must be correct?

options.A: The price of good X has increased relative to the price of good Y.
options.B: The prices of both goods have fallen.
options.C: There has been an increase in the consumer’s real income.
options.D: There has been an increase in the consumer’s money income.

questions.questionText: The short-run production function in the diagram shows the relationship between the total product of labour and labour hours worked. TPL output O labour hours What is held constant when drawing this function?

options.B: the hourly wage
options.C: the size of the labour force
options.D: the stock of capital

questions.questionText: What is an example of a wage differential that compensates for the disadvantages associated with particular jobs?

options.A: a tendency for wage rates negotiated by trade unions to exceed those for non-unionised labour
options.B: government office workers being paid more than private sector office workers
options.C: labourers on off-shore oil rigs earning more than those employed on-shore
options.D: male workers earning more than female workers in the same job

questions.questionText: To increase the labour force from 30 to 31 workers, an entrepreneur is forced to increase the daily wage rate from $40 to $41. What is the marginal cost of labour per day?
The workers in a firm have not previously belonged to a trade union but now join one. In which circumstance is this most likely to raise their wages?

options.A: Capital is highly substitutable for labour.
options.B: Labour costs constitute a large fraction of the firm’s costs.
options.C: The demand for the firm’s product is price-inelastic.
options.D: The firm operates in a perfectly competitive labour market.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the relationship between a firm’s output and the number of workers employed at different levels of capital stock (K). K K K output K O number employed What does the diagram show?

options.B: the firm’s long-run rate of return on capital
options.C: the firm’s long-run total cost function
options.D: the firm’s short-run rate of return on capital

questions.questionText: Which diagram shows the short-run marginal cost (MC) of providing a service where the total costs of production in the short run are fixed?

options.A: B C D MC MC costs costs costs costs MC MC O O O O number number number number of users of users of users of users

questions.questionText: Which is a financial economy of scale?

options.A: greater bargaining power in purchasing from suppliers
options.B: greater diversification of the product range
options.C: lower costs in raising capital
options.D: lower distribution costs by increasing market share

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a firm’s average revenue curve. revenue AR O output What can be deduced from the average revenue curve about the firm’s total revenue as it increases output?

options.B: It will fall continuously.
options.C: It will rise initially then fall.
options.D: It will fall initially then rise.

questions.questionText: What is an assumption underlying the kinked demand curve in oligopoly?

options.A: A firm will increase its price in response to a price increase by a rival.
options.B: A firm will not match a price cut by a rival.
options.C: Consumers are less sensitive to price increases than price decreases.
options.D: Rivals are expected to match any reduction in price.

questions.questionText: At its current level of output a monopolist is on the price-inelastic part of its demand curve. What would happen to price and output if it maximised its profits? price output

options.B: decrease increase
options.C: increase decrease
options.D: increase increase

questions.questionText: In many countries, laws exist which prohibit firms from copying innovations introduced by other firms. What is the economic reason behind these laws?

options.A: A degree of monopoly power can help to achieve allocative efficiency.
options.B: A degree of monopoly power may be helpful in achieving technical progress.
options.C: Research and development is best conducted by government organisations.
options.D: The prices of goods produced by monopolies need to be regulated.

questions.questionText: Which policy change will make some individuals better off without making anyone worse off?

options.A: allowing farmers to buy and sell milk quotas
options.B: introducing a national minimum wage
options.C: introducing free bus travel for those over 60
options.D: removing restrictions on the opening hours of supermarkets

questions.questionText: A good gives rise to external benefits and is produced under conditions of monopolistic competition. Which statement must be correct?

options.A: Output of the good is at the socially optimum level.
options.B: Output of the good is above the socially optimum level.
options.C: Private costs exceed social benefits.
options.D: Social benefits exceed private benefits.

questions.questionText: A woman joins the labour force earning a salary of $25000 per annum. Her partner, who is already employed, earns $18000 per annum. The couple pay a childminder $8000 per annum to look after their baby. What will be the increase in GDP?
A central bank purchases government securities as part of a policy of quantitative easing. What is likely to be the effect on interest rates and the supply of money? interest rates money supply

options.B: decrease increase
options.C: increase decrease
options.D: increase increase

questions.questionText: An economy is operating at its natural rate of unemployment. According to monetarist theory, what will be the effect of an unanticipated increase in the money supply on unemployment in the short run and in the long run? short run long run

options.B: no change reduction
options.C: reduction no change
options.D: reduction reduction

questions.questionText: In an economy in which there is full employment, the marginal propensity to consume of pensioners is greater than that of taxpayers. Government expenditure on pensions is decreased by $20 billion. To maintain full employment, taxation must be

options.B: increased by less than $20 billion.
options.C: reduced by less than $20 billion.
options.D: reduced by more than $20 billion.

What would be most likely to increase a country’s long-run trend rate of growth?

options.B: an increase in import tariffs
options.C: an increase in the money supply
options.D: a reduction in the ratio of Government Debt toGDP

questions.questionText: The chart shows the rates of economic growth and unemployment in a country for the period 2007 to 2010. percentage change in real GDP % 5 percentage rate of unemployment 2007 2008 2009 2010 year What does the chart show?

options.B: The standard of living fell between 2009 and 2010.
options.C: The total labour force declined between 2007 and 2009.
options.D: The unemployment rate fell when the growth rate increased.

questions.questionText: The number of people employed in a country and the level of unemployment both decrease. What could explain this?

options.A: an increase in the age at which state pensions are payable
options.B: an increase in the number of students
options.C: an increase in the population of working age
options.D: net inward immigration

questions.questionText: Which combination of government interventions would be intended to support the lower income group in an economy? welfare payment tax system type of subsidy system

options.B: means tested proportional private transport
options.C: universal proportional food
options.D: universal progressive private transport

questions.questionText: The government of a major trading country imposes a tariff on imported goods. What is likely to be the impact on the prices paid to the foreign producers of the goods and on the prices paid for the goods by domestic consumers? prices paid to prices paid by foreign domestic producers consumers

options.B: decrease increase
options.C: increase decrease
options.D: increase increase

questions.questionText: In which set of circumstances is an economy likely to experience both falling inflation and, at the same time, falling unemployment? unemployment actual growth rate in output

options.A: above the natural rate above long-term trend rate of growth
options.B: above the natural rate below long-term trend rate of growth
options.C: below the natural rate above long-term trend rate of growth
options.D: below the natural rate below long-term trend rate of growth
